dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: Overview of this orchestrator and the nodes it manages.
dashboard.setupIntro: Complete these steps to make the orchestrator production ready.
dashboard.stepMail: Configure the mail server for alerts

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.intro: Machines enrolled with this orchestrator. Approve new nodes, assign their role and keep an eye on them.
nodes.pendingIntro: Check that the fingerprint matches the one shown on the node before you approve it.
nodes.none: No nodes yet. Use Add node to install the client on a machine.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.rebootConfirm: Reboot {{name}}? If it is on air, the broadcast from this node stops until it is back.
nodes.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}}? The node has to be enrolled again to come back.
nodes.queued: Command sent. The node picks it up within a few seconds.
nodes.installIntro: Install the client on the machine, then approve it here.
nodes.afterInstall: The node then appears under Waiting for approval with a fingerprint. The same fingerprint is shown on the node (tvsm-agent status).
nodes.studio: Windows studio node (CasparCG + DeckLink + RTMP ingest)
nodes.studioHint: Run in PowerShell as Administrator. Installs the agent, CasparCG Server and the RTMP ingest server, and writes the CasparCG configuration. Fill in the media share and the management node address.

studio.title: Studio node
studio.installedAsHint: The installer set this node up as: {{role}}.
studio.installedAsDiffers: The role you picked is different.

atem.title: ATEM switchers
atem.intro: Every Blackmagic ATEM in the facility, with model, inputs and live tally. The orchestrator only watches: switching is done by the management node.
atem.name: Name
atem.hostHint: The orchestrator connects over the ATEM protocol (UDP 9910), just like ATEM Software Control.
atem.emptyHint: Add an ATEM by its IP address. Model, inputs and names are read from the device.
atem.neverSeen: The orchestrator has not reached this switcher yet. Check the IP address and that UDP port 9910 is open.
atem.offlineSnapshot: The switcher is offline. You are looking at the last known state.
atem.frontPanelHint: Click a source button to rename that input. The labels are written to the ATEM itself.
atem.frontPanelReadOnly: Live view of the switcher's source buttons and tally.
atem.noControl: Switching is done from the control panel below.
atem.inputsIntro: Names are read from and written to the switcher. "Fed by" records which node is connected to the input.
atem.namesHint: The long name appears in the multiview and ATEM Software Control, the short name on button labels of hardware panels. Letters, digits and basic punctuation only.
atem.fedByHint: Only stored in the orchestrator, for the equipment overview.
atem.offlineRename: The switcher is offline: names can only be changed while it is connected. You can still change the link and note.
atem.removeText: {{name}} is removed from the orchestrator. Nothing changes on the switcher itself.
atem.err_host_exists: A switcher with this address is already registered.
atem.err_atem_offline: The switcher is offline; try again when it is connected.
atem.err_unknown_input: This input does not exist on the switcher.
atem.err_forbidden: You do not have permission for this.
atem.err_validation_failed: Check the fields: names may only contain plain characters (long max 20, short max 4).
atem.err_invalid_me: This M/E or aux does not exist on the switcher.

control.title: Switching & automation
control.intro: Switch this ATEM by hand, or lock it so the management node's automation leaves it alone.
control.automationHint: The schedule on the management node switches this ATEM.
control.lockText: While locked, the automation on the management node does not switch this ATEM: the schedule keeps playing on the servers, but the picture on air is yours. When you release it, the automation takes the source the schedule wants at that moment, if it changed in the meantime.
control.offline: The switcher is offline: switching is not possible.
control.mayOverride: may switch again at the next item. Lock the ATEM to keep your choice.
control.askText: This ATEM is released to the automation, which may switch back at the next item in the schedule. Lock it first so your choice stays on air?
control.dontAsk: Don't ask again in this tab

automation.title: Automation link for management nodes
automation.intro: The management node asks the orchestrator every few seconds which ATEMs are locked. Enter this address and token on the management node under Devices → Orchestrator link.
automation.lastPoll: Last asked by a management node: {{at}} from {{ip}}
automation.neverPolled: No management node has asked yet.
automation.regenerateText: The old token stops working straight away. Management nodes keep their last known locks until you enter the new token there.

diagram.title: Connection diagram
diagram.intro: Which server, DeckLink output and other equipment is cabled to which ATEM input, and how the ATEMs feed each other. Live tally shows what is on air.
diagram.editingHint: Drag from an output (right) to an input (left) to draw a cable
diagram.help: Click an ATEM to switch it or lock it for the automation. Click a cable or device for details. Use Edit diagram to draw cables.
diagram.helpEdit: Drag devices to move them. Drag from a coloured output dot to an input dot to draw a cable; an input takes one cable. Select a device to edit its cards and ports.
diagram.empty: No devices on the diagram yet
diagram.emptyHint: Place your enrolled nodes and registered ATEMs, add cameras or converters, then draw the cables between their ports.
diagram.allNodesPlaced: All approved nodes are already on the diagram.
diagram.allAtemsPlaced: All registered ATEMs are already on the diagram.
diagram.name: Name
diagram.nameFromInventory: Leave empty to use the name from the inventory.
diagram.firstCardHint: You can add more cards and change ports later.
diagram.cardsHint: For example the DeckLink card in a server. Each output can be cabled to an ATEM input. For studio nodes, the CasparCG channel (ch) that plays on an output is shown on the diagram.
diagram.noCards: No cards yet. Edit the diagram to add one.
diagram.atemPortsHint: ATEM inputs and outputs come from the switcher itself, with the names you gave them under ATEM switchers.
diagram.atemUnknown: Not reached yet: the ports appear once the orchestrator has connected to this ATEM.
diagram.brokenLink: This cable is connected to a port that no longer exists (the ATEM reports fewer inputs, or the card changed).
diagram.brokenCount: {{count}} cable(s) on ports that no longer exist (dashed).
diagram.err_input_taken: That input already has a cable.
diagram.err_direction: A cable runs from an output to an input.
diagram.err_same_device: A cable must go to another device.
diagram.err_already_placed: That one is already on the diagram.
diagram.allTeranexPlaced: Every Teranex is already on the diagram.
diagram.teranexPortsHint: The connectors come from the Teranex model (SDI, HDMI and optical in and out). You can still adjust them afterwards.

teranex.title: Teranex converters
teranex.intro: Blackmagic Teranex converters in the facility. The orchestrator only reads their status (input, format, audio, output); settings are changed on the device itself.
teranex.hostHint: IP address of the Teranex. The orchestrator connects on TCP port 9800 (Teranex Ethernet Protocol) and only reads.
teranex.expectedHint: For example 1080i50. When the input carries another format you get a warning and a mail. Empty = no check.
teranex.emptyHint: Add a Teranex with its IP address. Model, input and output are read from the device.
teranex.neverSeen: The orchestrator has not reached this Teranex yet. Check the IP address, that the device is on and that TCP port 9800 is reachable from the orchestrator.
teranex.readOnly: Read only: the orchestrator never changes settings on this Teranex. It sits in the live chain, so changes are made on the front panel or in Teranex Setup.
teranex.signalPathIntro: What goes in and what comes out, as the device reports it. Changes made on the front panel show up here within a second.
teranex.label: Label
teranex.allSettingsIntro: Every status block the Teranex sends, exactly as received. For reference only.
teranex.removeText: Remove {{name}} from the orchestrator? Nothing changes on the device itself.
teranex.err_host_exists: A Teranex with this address is already registered.
teranex.err_unknown_teranex: This Teranex is not in the inventory.
teranex.offlineSnapshot: The Teranex is offline. You see the last known state.

mon.title: Monitoring
mon.intro: Status of the whole platform at a glance: the orchestrator, TV studios, switchers, converters, distribution and other equipment. Refreshes every 5 seconds.
mon.noDist: Add the Owncast server that serves the web stream on the website to see whether it is live and how many people are watching.
mon.noExtra: Nothing added yet. Add for example the NAS, a converter, a tally box or the UPS.
mon.check_tcp_hint: OK when the port accepts a connection
mon.target_owncast_hint: The Owncast web address, e.g. http://10.40.6.127:8080. Only the public status is read; nothing is changed.
mon.target_http_hint: Full URL; any answer below 400 counts as OK.
mon.target_tcp_hint: host:port, e.g. 10.40.0.154:445 for an SMB share.
mon.agentHint: If the TVSM agent runs on this machine (e.g. the Linux server with Owncast), link it to also see CPU, memory, disk and whether the agent answers.
mon.problemsIntro: Everything that is not OK right now, most serious first.
mon.err_invalid_target: This address is not valid for the chosen check.

issue.mail_not_configured: Mail server not configured: alerts are not sent
issue.backup_old: No successful backup in the last 8 days

mon.layerDesc_distribution: Web stream, website and other outlets
mon.layerDesc_infrastructure: Servers, storage, power and other equipment
mon.pathHint: Click a layer to show only that layer
mon.hint3d: Drag to rotate, click a block for details
mon.noSelection: Select something to see its details.
